data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Evidence within a single evaluation distinguishes genuine from compliance-driven reliability only if the evaluation includes a corrupted-checklist or shuffled-criteria control: if the panel's advantage survives intact when the checklist's rules are silently degraded, the advantage is not checklist-mediated.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The real-checklist and corrupted-checklist sub-panels perform identically, indicating the checklist's content is irrelevant to the advantage.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The corrupted-checklist sub-panel outperforms the expert (the panel advantage is driven by panel composition or task framing, not checklist content).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The control is not feasible within a single evaluation (e.g., the panel cannot be meaningfully split, or corruption is detectable).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The real-checklist sub-panel does not outperform the expert (the checklist provides no genuine advantage).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The most direct single-evaluation discriminating test is an internal counterfactual: split the panel into sub-panels, give one the real checklist and the other a corrupted version (shuffled criteria, reversed thresholds, or placebo rules). If only the real-checklist sub-panel outperforms the expert, the checklist's specific content is causally responsible. If both outperform equally, the panel's advantage is not checklist-mediated (it is a panel-composition or mere-compliance effect). This is the strongest design because it holds panel composition and case-difficulty constant while varying only checklist validity.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
